name: FlexGen: High-Throughput Generative Inference of Large Language Models with a Single GPU
problem: Serving a large model on a single commodity GPU requires offloading weights and KV cache to CPU, disk and even across GPUs, and that offloading is dominated by I/O and memory-transfer latency rather than arithmetic, so throughput collapses.
mechanism: A constrained scheduling framework that treats a single-GPU + CPU (+ disk) hierarchy as the whole machine and solves a LINEAR PROGRAMMING problem for the best plan jointly: which GPU operators run per iteration, whether each layer's weights are prefetched / computed / discarded on the CPU, and where the attention KV cache lives. Weights and the attention cache are additionally compressed to 4 bits with their own quantization scheme so more state fits on the GPU. The plan is searched per model and device rather than hand-tuned.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim: up to 4x higher throughput than HuggingFace Accelerate with a 13B model and OPT-175B on a single 16GB A100, by using a discount policy on the offloaded KV cache; and 1-4x higher effective batch size. Numbers are per-GPU and depend on the offload hierarchy.
notes: Added as the load-bearing 2023 offload-scheduling paper: the repo has PowerInfer-style consumer-GPU offload and Tetra, but nothing that formalises offload scheduling as a joint policy over compute-vs-transfer-vs-cache-placement, which is the actual mechanism behind why a single GPU can serve a big model at all. Venue ICML 2023, verified against the PMLR v202 table of contents (v202 confirmed as the 40th ICML, 23-29 July 2023, by reading the volume landing page header rather than assuming the volume-to-year mapping).
